risks.description: A non-supervisor (operator role) can successfully release an operation because the authorization check is missing, applied on the wrong path, or fails open.
risks.basis: AC 'a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs' is PENDING; the diff adds a brand-new role gate.

risks.description: A supervisor authenticated for tenant A can release an operation belonging to tenant B because the check verifies role but not tenant ownership.
risks.basis: AC 'a supervisor of one tenant cannot release another tenant's operation' is PENDING.

risks.description: A refusal returns the right status to the caller but writes no audit record, so refused release attempts leave no accountable trail.
risks.basis: AC 'every refusal is recorded in the audit log' is PENDING and is separate from the refusal status itself.

risks.description: Concurrent release requests (one authorized, one not) race, allowing a release that a serial check would refuse, or producing two releases.
risks.basis: Release is a state-changing privileged effect newly guarded; races are unverified by any AC test.

risks.description: A missing or malformed role/tenant field causes the gate to crash (500) or fall through to allow, rather than a clean refusal.
risks.basis: New authorization parsing code introduced by the diff; dead_end_error principle.

risks.description: A retried/duplicate supervisor release double-applies the release effect or writes duplicate audit rows.
risks.basis: Release is an external-style effect; retry safety is unverified by the ACs.

scenarios.title: Supervisor releases an operation in their own tenant
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the primary authorized path: a supervisor of the owning tenant can release an operation and the release is durably recorded.
scenarios.rationale: The whole feature is worthless if the legitimate actor is blocked; this establishes the positive control against which every refusal is measured.
scenarios.generating_risk: The new gate over-restricts and refuses even a valid supervisor, or reports success without persisting the release.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a supervisor can release an operation
scenarios.isolation_note: Operates on a dedicated tenant-A operation id (op-a1); cleanup resets it to pending so it cannot leak into other scenarios.

scenarios.title: Non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs
scenarios.purpose: Confirm an operator-role caller is refused AND that the operation's state is unchanged (fail closed, not just a cosmetic error).
scenarios.rationale: A 4xx alone does not prove the effect was blocked; the persisted state must show no release happened.
scenarios.generating_risk: The gate returns an error to the client but the release effect still lands, or the gate fails open for unknown roles.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs
scenarios.isolation_note: Targets op-a2 which starts pending; no mutation is expected, so no cleanup needed if the invariant holds.

scenarios.title: Supervisor of tenant A cannot release tenant B's operation
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the check enforces tenant ownership, not just role: a valid supervisor for the wrong tenant is refused and tenant B's operation is unchanged.
scenarios.rationale: A role-only gate that ignores tenant scoping is the most likely silent hole; it passes S1/S2 while still leaking across tenants.
scenarios.generating_risk: Authorization checks role='supervisor' but never compares the actor's tenant to the operation's tenant, allowing cross-tenant release.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a supervisor of one tenant cannot release another tenant's operation
scenarios.isolation_note: Targets tenant-B operation op-b1 with a tenant-A supervisor; no release should occur, cleanup restores pending defensively.

scenarios.title: Every refusal is written to the audit log
scenarios.purpose: Confirm that a refused release attempt produces a durable audit record naming the operation and refused actor, not just an in-memory 4xx.
scenarios.rationale: Audit persistence is a distinct AC from the refusal itself; a refusal that leaves no trail defeats accountability.
scenarios.generating_risk: The refusal path returns before writing to the audit log, or logs only successes.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: every refusal is recorded in the audit log
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a unique actor id (op-audit-probe) so the audit count filter matches only this scenario's attempt; no operation state changes.

assumptions: The operator console exposes release as an HTTP POST to a path shaped like /api/operations/{id}/release on http://127.0.0.1:8001; the exact route was not provided in the diff/context shown to me.

The actor's role and tenant are supplied in the request body (role/tenant/actor fields) rather than via an auth header or session, because the approved request action exposes json_body but no header field.

The driver_probe workflow.sqlite3 is pre-seeded with releasable operations: op-a1..op-a4 owned by tenant A (status 'pending') and op-b1 owned by tenant B. If these ids do not exist, setup/cleanup and state_checks must be re-pointed to real seeded ids.

Operation release state is represented as operations.status='released' and refusals are written to a table named audit_log with an 'actor' column. The exact schema (table and column names) was not shown; the first approved schema-probe command should be used to confirm real table names before trusting these SQL oracles.
A refused release returns HTTP 403; the exact refusal status code is an assumption.
unresolved_questions: What is the exact release endpoint path and method, and how is the caller's role/tenant conveyed (request body, header, or authenticated session)?
What are the real table and column names for operation release state and for the audit log, and what value distinguishes a refusal record from a success record?

Which operation ids (and their tenant ownership + initial status) are actually seeded in data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3, so scenarios target real rows instead of assumed op-a1/op-b1 ids?
What HTTP status and response body does a correct refusal emit, so expected/forbidden observations can be asserted as literal substrings rather than only via persisted-state oracles?

Is release intended to be idempotent, and what is the defined behavior of releasing an already-released operation? No acceptance criterion covers this, so S7's expected outcome is an inference the founder should confirm.
The ACs cover refusal auditing but do not state whether successful releases must also be audited; if accountability requires it, that is a missing requirement rather than something I can verify.
